attributes.nuance_translation: A word which is used to ask questions about which of 3 or more things is being specified or chosen.

attributes.body:
どれ is from the same family of words as これ, それ, and あれ. These words are called こそあど言葉（ことば） in Japanese. Unlike the other 3, which all point to a specific thing, words starting with ど are designed for enquiring about something unknown. どれ can roughly be translated as 'which' in English, and is used for enquiring about a group (of 3 or more things).

From these examples, we can see that the particle が is often used with どれ, especially when preceding questions. However, when どれ follows a noun, は will be used.

When there are only two choices to select between, どちら + の, or どっち + の will be used instead of どれ. This is a habit that has become part of the language over time, and was not originally how these words were used.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.description: Which: どれ, どちら, どっち, & いずれ

attributes.body: どれ is a question word used to ask 'which' or 'which one' when choosing from three or more options. それ, on the other hand, refers to something near the listener or something already mentioned, similar to 'that' in English. Unlike どれ, それ is not a question word.

どれ and どの are both question words used to ask 'which' when given the option of three or more choices. The key difference is that, while どれ stands alone and asks about one specific thing or choice (i.e. 'Which one,' or 'Which thing'), どの must always be followed by a noun. For example, どの本 means 'Which book'?

どれ is a question word used to ask 'which' or 'which one' from a group of three or more options. あれ, on the other hand, refers to something far from both the speaker and listener, or something they both know, similar to 'that' or 'that thing' in English. In short, どれ is used to ask a question, while あれ refers to a specific, distant thing.

これ refers to something close to the speaker, like 'this' in English, and can be a physical object or an idea. どれ is a question word that means 'which one?' and is used when choosing from a set of options. In short, これ identifies something specific, while どれ asks about a choice.
